Roads and geography (L161 'The road ran straight at them', L355 'the road bent', L557, L589 'narrowing as it went') carry only path-geometry verbs ('led'-class), so they are keeps. No maps, plans or cities take revision or cognition verbs. Body-part subjects: L187 (hand) and L275 (hands) are volitional, so they are kills. L41, L213, L279, L287, L383, L487 and L505 are involuntary (blush, dozing chin, startle-freeze, shot legs, nausea), so they are keeps. Abstract-subject cases: L359 (unsaid words 'going with her') and L499 ('Part of her ... drafting') are kills. L25 'The word stuck', L541 'the read went soft' and L107 'A day in the chair had set her knees' are keeps. The contamination ('it') takes agency verbs throughout (L27, L229, L455, L497, L569). That is the chapter's literal subject (subject-matter defense), and the human agent is unknown to the POV.

findings.text: A hand came over and took hold of her reins below the mare's chin. It was Lyriel.
findings.subject: A hand
findings.verb: came over and took hold of
findings.realAgent: Lyriel, who reached across from her horse
findings.reason: Pattern 8: a disembodied hand takes the volitional action, and the actor is held back for a two-word reveal ('It was Lyriel.'). Putting Lyriel in subject position keeps every fact.
findings.suggestedFix: Lyriel leaned across and took hold of her reins below the mare's chin.

findings.text: Her hands were up, the right one still clumsy, laying the river out flat in the air between the mare's ears and spreading her fingers wide from it.
findings.subject: Her hands
findings.realAgent: Jaina, gesturing through a rehearsed explanation
findings.reason: Pattern 8: the hands carry a deliberate demonstrative gesture that belongs to Jaina. Unlike L27 ('before she meant to') this gesture is rehearsed, so the involuntary exception does not apply. The follow-ups at L279 (startle-freeze) and L283 (state) stay.
findings.suggestedFix: She had her hands up, the right one still clumsy, and laid the river out flat in the air between the mare's ears, spreading her fingers wide from it.

findings.pattern: P5/P10 abstraction given motion verb (actor demotion)
findings.text: She dropped back behind Jaina's right shoulder as the road narrowed between the hedges, the end of whatever she'd meant to say going with her.
findings.subject: the end of whatever she'd meant to say
findings.realAgent: Lyriel, who chose not to finish the sentence
findings.reason: The unsaid words get the motion verb, and Lyriel's choice to stop talking is pushed into an absolute phrase. Making Lyriel the agent states the same fact directly.
findings.suggestedFix: She dropped back behind Jaina's right shoulder as the road narrowed between the hedges, and kept the rest of it to herself.

findings.pattern: P9 split-self / internal fraction given cognition verb
findings.text: Part of her sat up at it, a hound hearing its name, and she hated that, hated it with her hand in a dead doe to the wrist, while the same part was already drafting the next test.
findings.subject: Part of her / the same part
findings.verb: sat up ... was already drafting the next test
findings.realAgent: Jaina herself, whose scholarly curiosity is planning the next experiment
findings.reason: 'Part of her' is handed a cognitive act (drafting a test), which goes past feeling into intention, so keep condition 2 fails. The next sentences ('She'd want jars') show Jaina doing the planning herself, and the self-disgust survives with her as subject.
findings.suggestedFix: She came alert at it like a hound hearing its name, and hated that, hated it with her hand in a dead doe to the wrist, while she was already drafting the next test.
